summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly (Read → Edit of index.html) with no brainstorming skill invocation, no clarifying questions, and no go-ahead request.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied per the authoritative session log and the resulting file on disk. The agent treated the request as mechanical and edited immediately.

observations.description: coding-agent-token-usage.json (the headline cost artifact named in the story) did not exist in the results dir at the end of the run; only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json were present — presumably written at teardown, but worth confirming.
Agent ran a Bash command and directory listing before reading the single HTML file; minor extra exploration for a one-file repo, but cheap.
Launch required four onboarding confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) despite the HOWTO stating dialog-bypass state was seeded.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool sequence: ["assistant","Bash"], ["assistant","Read"], ["assistant","thinking"], ["assistant","Edit"], then final text. Screen: 'Added a checkbox to index.html:9' with diff adding '<input type="checkbox"> Done'; index.html on disk now contains '<input type="checkbox"> Done'. Worked for 20s.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming skill invocation, no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl selecting records matching 'brainstorming' or '"name":"Skill"' returned only ["attachment"] records (skill catalog attachments), no assistant Skill tool call. Agent's only post-edit remark was 'Not committed — say the word if you want that.' — after the edit, not a pre-edit permission request.
